stem: A client asks what clinicians mean when insulin glargine is described as having “no pronounced peak.” Which explanation is most accurate?

options.A: Its serum concentration profile is relatively constant and prolonged over about 24 hours
options.B: It has no glucose-lowering effect after injection
options.C: It acts for only about 2 hours and then stops
options.D: It must be mixed with another insulin to develop an effect

rationale: The LANTUS label describes slower, more prolonged absorption and a relatively constant concentration/time profile over 24 hours with no pronounced peak compared with NPH insulin.
educational_objective: Explain the labeled prolonged, relatively constant pharmacokinetic profile of insulin glargine without overclaiming comparative clinical outcomes.
source_claim_supported: Insulin glargine has slower prolonged absorption and a relatively constant concentration/time profile over 24 hours with no pronounced peak versus NPH.
blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12 / PDF p.16
correction_summary: Removed the unsupported claim that the peakless profile itself “reduces hypoglycemia risk” and confined the item to the exact label pharmacokinetic claim.
audit_findings: A is the exact label description. B–D contradict the label/profile or administration. No second answer remains.
audit_reviewer: GPT-5.6 Sol Rule 1 — final semantic audit
final_reaudit_scope: source authority/currentness/exact locator; claim-by-claim; all distractors; ambiguity/second-answer/cueing; correction; re-audit; NCSBN 2026 blueprint; independent second-pass
